title: Kernel arbitration and decode backpressure controller
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Implement an adaptive kernel arbitration layer plus a decode backpressure controller that reduces latency spikes and kernel oscillation during mixed workloads. The goal is to prioritize latency-sensitive small requests while preserving throughput for batchy workloads through graceful backpressure signaling to the scheduler and decode pipeline. This ticket covers design, prototype, experiments, and a phased rollout with telemetry and rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: New arbitration module routes requests using an urgency score (latency SLO, tokens remaining, tenant priority) and exposes a per-device queue watermark
Decode pacing controller can delay token emission by up to configurable ms thresholds and reduce batch formation aggressiveness under backpressure
99th percentile tail latency for small (<64 tokens) requests reduces by at least 25% under mixed load compared to baseline
System-level oscillations (kernel handoffs) reduced: measured drop in kernel-swap events per minute by >30% during burst tests
Canary deployment path and automated rollback when error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds
implementation_plan: Design: define urgency score, queue watermarks, and control loop; produce cost/latency tradeoff doc
Prototype: implement arbitration shim in serving runtime between ingress and kernel scheduler; instrument signals to emit telemetry
Integrate decode backpressure controller to influence batch formation and token emission rate (streaming path) via token pacing and early flush heuristics
Bench: synthetic mixed-workload harness (small interactive + large batch) in perf lab, run parameter sweep on watermarks and pacing thresholds
Canary: stage rollout on 5% traffic with per-tenant opt-out, monitor dashboards and runbooks
Rollout: ramp to 25%/50%/100% subject to telemetry gates; ship runtime flag and runtime-1.21 release note
experiments: Burst test: 1k rps of 32-token requests + 200 rps of 2048-token batched requests over 30m; compare baseline vs arbitration enabled
Watermark sensitivity: low/medium/high queue watermarks and their effect on kernel-swap frequency and decode latency
Pacing granularity: token-level pacing (per-token delay) vs chunk-level pacing (emit in 8-token chunks) for streaming clients
Tenant QoS: simulate high-priority tenant and ensure guaranteed latency under contention
telemetry: New metrics: kernel_arbitrator.route_decision, kernel_arbitrator.urgency_score, device.queue_depth_watermark, decode_pacing.delay_ms
Dashboards: per-tenant tail latency, kernel-swap rate, throughput loss, error rate; compare canary vs baseline cohorts
Alerting: sustained 99p latency increase >15% for 5 minutes => auto-rollback trigger
risks: Over-aggressive pacing could increase P50 latency for throughput-focused workloads
Incorrect urgency scoring might starve batch jobs leading to throughput cliffs
Complexity in kernel scheduler interactions could surface new deadlocks or increased memory pressure
Need to ensure backpressure signals do not cascade to client disconnects for streaming sessions
